rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative implies Mary remained in the Temple’s service and worshiped in a private mihrab; Zakariya visited her and saw out-of-season fruit as a miracle for her.
rows.anchor: فكانت مريم ملازمة لخدمة بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kullamā combines kull, a noun of generality, with temporal mā and its implied verbal clause: every time Zakariya entered, he found provision.
rows.anchor: الذي هو اسم لعموم ما يضاف هو إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “he found provision with her” can be parsed as a circumstantial clause describing Zakariya in the preceding account of his guardianship.
rows.anchor: حال من زكرياء في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the clause about finding provision can be an appositional complement of the guardianship clause, specifying an aspect of it.
rows.anchor: بدل اشتمال من جملة { وكفلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mihrab is a structure made for solitary worship and prayer, usually raised and reached by steps; it is distinct from a mosque.
rows.anchor: بناء يتخذه أحد ليخلو فيه بتعبده وصلاته

rows.speaker: عمر بن أبي ربيعة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Rabiʿa uses mihrab expansively for a church’s sanctuary or altar, although a mihrab is not literally where an altar is placed.
rows.anchor: كقول عمر بن أبي ربيعة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed etymology derives mihrab from ḥarb, treating the worshipper as one who battles Satan in that place.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل : إن المحراب مشتق من الحرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims later used mihrab for the prayer niche at the qibla where the imam stands; this was a later, developed usage.
rows.anchor: ثم أطلق المحراب عند المسلمين على موضع كشكل نصف قبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first Islamic mihrab was in the Prophet’s Mosque, built under al-Walid ibn ʿAbd al-Malik while ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz governed Medina.
rows.anchor: وأول محراب في الإسلام محراب مسجد الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم صنع في خلافة الوليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in “the mihrab” is generic; context identifies it as the worship niche Mary had made for herself.
rows.anchor: تعريف الجنس ويعلم أن المراد محراب جعلته مريم للتعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anā asks about place and means “from where”; Mary’s answer, “from God,” directly answers Zakariya’s question.
rows.anchor: أي من أين لك هذا ، فلذلك كان جواب استفهامه قوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Zakariya asked because the food appeared out of season; one report identifies it as grapes in winter.
rows.anchor: قيل : كان عنبا في فصل الشتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence “God provides for whom He wills” is part of Mary’s quoted speech.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إن الله يرزق من يشاء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥisāb here suggests limitation: God provides an amount whose measure is unknown, since it depends on His bounty rather than a counted allotment.
rows.anchor: بمعنى الحصر لأن الحساب يقتضي حصر الشيء المحسوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning of rizq was explained earlier in the commentary on God providing whom He wills without measure.
rows.anchor: والرزق تقدم آنفا عند قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “There” means in that place, before Zakariya left it.
rows.anchor: أي في المكان ، قبل أن يخرج

words: رب هب لي من لدنك ذرية طيبة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing Mary’s extraordinary provision and hearing her words in 3:37 prompted the childless, distressed Zakariya to ask for a child despite his old age and the unlikely timing.
rows.anchor: وقد نبهه إلى الدعاء مشاهدة خوارق العادة

words: رب هب لي من لدنك ذرية طيبة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya asks for good progeny because he expects them to bring beneficial effects and good in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: وسأل الذرية الطيبة لأنها التي يرجى منها خير الدنيا والآخرة

words: رب هب لي من لدنك ذرية طيبة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The observed miracles made it proper to request an extraordinary or improbable gift: Zakariya felt close to divine care in a place and time of divine effusion, without breaching the etiquette of supplication described by al-Qarafi.
rows.anchor: ومشاهدة خوارق العادات خولت لزكرياء الدعاء بما هو من الخوارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samīʿ means “responsive” here, rather than merely hearing.
rows.anchor: وسميع هنا معنى مجيب .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa in the angels’ calling marks immediate succession: the prayer was answered at once.
rows.anchor: للتعقيب أي استجيبت دعوته للوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the explanation in 4:26, this verse reminds the community that God continues to intend ease and care for it.
rows.anchor: بالتذكير بأن الله لا يزال مراعيا رفقه بهذه الأمة وإرادته بها اليسر دون العسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The law balances securing benefits and averting harms gently; it can waive some harms when avoiding them would impose hardship or block a benefit, as with permission for those unable to afford free women to marry enslaved women.
rows.anchor: فربما ألغت الشريعة بعض المفاسد إذا كان في الحمل على تركها مشقة أو تعطيل مصلحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The principle of ease is reinforced by verses denying hardship, preferring ease, and lifting burdens from earlier communities.
rows.anchor: والآيات الدالة على هذا المعنى بلغت مبلغ القطع كقوله : { وما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج }

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith the author calls authentic says this religion is easy and whoever makes it burdensome will be overcome by it.
rows.anchor: في الحديث الصحيح : ( إن هذا الدين يسر ولن يشاد هذا الدين أحد إلا غلبه )

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet instructed Muʿadh and Abu Musa to make matters easy and not difficult.
rows.anchor: فقال لمعاذ وأبي موسى : ( يسرا ولا تعسرا )

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that his envoys had been sent as bearers of good news, not as people who repel others.
rows.anchor: وقال : ( إنما بعثتم مبشرين لا منفرين )

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When Muʿadh complained about an imam who prolonged prayer, the Prophet rebuked him with “Are you putting people to trial?”
rows.anchor: وقال لمعاذ لما شكا بعض المصلين خلفه من تطويله ( أفتان أنت )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ease is a foundational principle of Islamic law from which the two kinds of legal concessions branch.
rows.anchor: فكان التيسير من أصول الشريعة الإسلامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that humanity was created weak is a concluding generalization and a rationale for easing; it presents Islam as especially suited to people in every time and place, unlike earlier religions that addressed particular conditions.
rows.anchor: وإظهار لمزية هذا الدين وأنه أليق الأديان بالناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is linked to the declaration that God has now lightened the burden because He knows the believers are weak.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا المعنى قوله تعالى : { الآن خفف الله عنكم وعلم أن فيكم ضعفا

rows.speaker: طاووس
rows.claim: Tawus says a person is weaker in no matter than in the matter of women; Ibn ʿAshur says this is included but does not exhaust the verse’s meaning, since some rulings eased marriage.
rows.anchor: قال طاووس ليس يكون الإنسان في شيء أضعف منه في أمر النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening address marks a new section of legislation; after inheritance and marriage rules about giving rights in property, the sura turns to general laws concerning property and lives.
rows.anchor: استئناف من التشريع المقصود من هذه السورة . وعلامة الاستئناف افتتاحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Eating” is a conventionalized metaphor for full appropriation; eating wealth falsely means seizing it with no intention to return it, usually by injustice.
rows.anchor: فأكل الأموال هو الاستيلاء عليها بنية عدم إرجاعها لأربابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor can also cover permitted use, as in a wife’s willing gift or a guardian’s customary use; this is why prohibited appropriation is qualified by “wrongfully.”
rows.anchor: وغالب هذا المعنى أن يكون استيلاء ظلم ، وهو مجاز صار كالحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject pronoun of “eat” and the possessive pronoun in “your wealth” refer to the believers collectively, so the sense is that they must not consume one another’s property.
rows.anchor: وظاهر أن المرء لا ينهى عن أكل مال نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bāṭil is the opposite of right: what God has not legislated and what the property owner has not permitted; the bāʾ indicates association or circumstance.
rows.anchor: والباطل ضد الحق ، وهو ما لم يشرعه الله ولا كان عن إذن ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAshur prefers a disconnected exception: trade is not wrongful consumption, and the exception means that trade is not prohibited; this fits Arabic without implying exclusivity.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء في قوله : { إلا أن تكون تجارة } منقطع ، لأن التجارة ليست من أكل الأموال بالباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, if “wrongfully” is treated as inoperative in the exception, the exception is connected, but that would wrongly imply trade is the only permitted way to use wealth.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يجعل قيد { الباطل } في حالة الاستثناء ملغى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trade is singled out because profit can make it resemble wrongful taking, yet commerce is permitted because merchants circulate needed and desirable goods that people otherwise could not obtain.
rows.anchor: وأما التجارة فلأجل ما فيها من أخذ المتصدي للتجر ما لا زائدا على قيمة ما بذله للمشتري

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Al-Muwattaʾ reports ʿUmar saying that an importer who brings food through winter and summer is his guest and may sell or hold it as he wishes.
rows.anchor: في ( الموطأ ) عن عمر بن الخطاب أنه قال : في احتكار الطعام

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers put tijāratun in the nominative as subject of complete kāna, meaning “trade occurs.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { إلا أن تكون تجارة } برفع تجارة على أنه فاعل

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: ʿAsim, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Khalaf read tijāratan in the accusative as the predicate of incomplete kāna, with “wealth” as its implied subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأه عاصم ، وحمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف بنصب تجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase qualifies trade: ʿan indicates that the transaction issues from mutual consent, shown by words or customary conduct.
rows.anchor: و ( عن ) فيه للمجاوزة ، أي صادرة عن التراضي وهو الرضا من الجانبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik uses the verse to support denying the buyer or seller an option to cancel while still at the market: consent is realized through offer and acceptance.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية ما يصلح أن يكون مستندا لقول مالك من نفي خيار المجلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is a major foundation for the inviolability of property, echoed in the Prophetic rule that a Muslim’s property is lawful only with willing consent.
rows.anchor: أصل عظيم في حرمة الأموال

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the Farewell Pilgrimage sermon, the Prophet declared people’s blood and property inviolable.
rows.anchor: وفي خطبة حجة الوداع ( إن دماءكم وأموالكم عليكم حرام )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Property is mentioned before killing, despite the latter’s greater danger, either because the prior context concerned property or because people recently out of jāhiliyya more readily exploited the vulnerable than committed murder.
rows.anchor: وتقديم النهي عن أكل الأموال على النهي عن قتل الأنفس ، مع أن الثاني أخطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People could exploit orphans, women, and wives with relative impunity because victims were weak; murder, by contrast, triggered retaliation even against the powerful, since tribes did not ignore their dead.
rows.anchor: وكان أكل الأموال أسهل عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural prohibition means that people must not kill one another; suicide is also included, since God did not authorize people to destroy themselves, but suicide is not the verse’s sole meaning.
rows.anchor: قوله : { ولا تقتلوا أنفسكم } نهي عن أن يقتل الرجل غيره

rows.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: In the expedition of Dhat al-Salasil, ʿAmr performed tayammum in severe cold instead of bathing, led the prayer, and invoked this verse; the Prophet did not object, supporting its general wording.
rows.anchor: أن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنه تيمم في يوم شديد البرد ولم يغتسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Whoever does that” refers to the two preceding acts: consuming wealth wrongfully and killing.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { ومن يفعل ذلك } أي المذكور : من أكل المال بالباطل والقتل

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says “that” may instead refer to the earlier prohibition on inheriting women against their will in 4:19, since it receives no later threat and is preceded by a warning.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الإشارة إلى ما ذكر من قوله تعالى : { يأيها الذين آمنوا لا يحل لكم أن ترثوا النساء كرها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualification “aggression and wrongdoing” excludes rightful appropriation or killing, such as lawful retaliation.
rows.anchor: وإنما قيده بالعدوان والظلم ليخرج أكل المال بوجه الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUdwan with ḍamma is a verbal noun on the pattern of kufrān; with kasra it can mean forceful domination, usually unjust but sometimes rightful, as 2:193 shows. Ẓulm is a specific instance of the general term.
rows.anchor: والعدوان بضم العين مصدر بوزن كفران ، ويقال بكسر العين وهو التسلط بشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the stronger grammatical view, sawfa marks the future just as sīn does; some grammarians say it indicates the distant future, but usage provides no evidence for that claim.
rows.anchor: حرف يدخل على المضارع فيمحضه للزمن المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṣlīhi means “make him enter the fire” or “make him burn.”
rows.anchor: و ( نصليه ) نجعله صاليا أو محترقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning establishes two necessary objectives of Islamic law: preservation of property and preservation of life.
rows.anchor: وهما حفظ الأموال ، وحفظ الأنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause coordinates with the command not to advocate for the treacherous in 4:105; divine favor here is the revelation that clarifies correct judgment and protects the Prophet from error in it.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته لهمت طائفة منهم أن يضلوك } عطف على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is that the faction’s attempt to mislead the Prophet never even arose, much less succeeded: public knowledge of his honesty prevented them from confidently trying to pass off a lie.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية أن هم طائفة من الذين يختانون أنفسهم بأن يضلون الرسول غير واقع من أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In one account, Banu Zufr complained to the Prophet about Qatada ibn al-Nuʿman and his uncle while believing Banu Ubayriq were in the right.
rows.anchor: وأن بني ظفر لما اشتكوا إليه من صنيع قتادة بن النعمان وعمه كانوا يظنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Banu Ubayriq complained about Qatada while fearing that God would disclose the facts to the Prophet; their bid was hopeful, not a firm resolve, since ham implies determination and confidence.
rows.anchor: أو أن بني أبيرق لما شكوا إلى رسول الله بما صنعه قتادة كانوا موجسين خيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the verse to deny only the effect of their attempt, meaning God prevented the Prophet from being misled; Ibn ʿAshur rejects this as weak in both wording and meaning.
rows.anchor: وقيل في تفسير هذا الانتفاء : إن المراد انتفاء أثره ، أي لولا فضل الله لضللت بهمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Any attempted deception would mislead the plotters themselves: they would deserve error for trying to promote falsehood, while the Prophet would not heed it.
rows.anchor: ومعنى : { وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم } أنهم لو هموا بذلك لكان الضلال لاحقا بهم دونك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min in the denial of harm is augmentative and reinforces the negation.
rows.anchor: و { من } زائدة لتأكيد النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shayʾ would originally be accusative as an absolute object meaning “any harm,” but it is genitive because it follows the augmentative preposition.
rows.anchor: و { شيء } أصله النصب على أنه مفعول مطلق لقوله { يضرونك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation clause coordinates with the statement that they cannot harm the Prophet, further establishing the earlier divine favor; the final mention of great favor echoes the opening (ring composition).
rows.anchor: وجملة : { وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب والحكمة } عطف على { وما يضرونك من شيء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is the Qurʾan, wisdom is Prophethood, and the knowledge taught beyond the Book includes the Sunna and reports of unseen matters.
rows.anchor: والكتاب : والقرآن . والحكمة : النبوءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAshur rejects two reported occasions for a plot to kill the Prophet: Banu Nadir’s plan when he sought blood money, and a Bedouin’s attempt to seize his sword while he slept; neither fits the verse’s plural group address.
rows.anchor: ما يذكر من غير هذا مما هم به بنو النضير من قتل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report of a Bedouin who drew the Prophet’s sword while he was resting on return from an expedition is also unsuitable, since it involves one would-be killer rather than a group.
rows.anchor: وكذا ما يذكر من أن المراد قصة الأعرابي الذي اخترط سيف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bast al-yad is figurative for violence or force, as in the threat to extend hands and tongues against people.
rows.anchor: وبسط اليد مجاز في البطش قال تعالى : { ويبسطوا إليكم أيديهم وألسنتهم بالسوء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same expression can figuratively mean having authority or power over others, or being generous, as in the verse about God’s outstretched hands.
rows.anchor: كما في قوله تعالى : { بل يداه مبسوطتان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the sons of Adam passage, extending a hand is literal: an attempt to seize or grasp someone.
rows.anchor: وهو حقيقة في محاولة الإمساك بشيء ، كما في قوله تعالى حكاية عن ابن آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaff al-yad, “withholding the hand,” is a metaphor for turning away specifically from evil.
rows.anchor: وأما كف اليد فهو مجاز عن الإعراض عن السوء خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God after recalling His favor is both an evident form of gratitude and an independent aim, indicated by coordination with wāw.
rows.anchor: والأمر بالتقوى عقب ذلك لأنها أظهر للشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The two sons of Adam” means his two sons; “son of Adam” in the singular can mean one human being, while the plural can address humanity collectively.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { ابني آدم } هنا ولداه . وأما ابن آدم مفردا فقد يراد به واحد من البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-l-ḥaqq may mean truthfully and accurately: truth is established reality, unlike falsehood, as in the account of the youths of the cave.
rows.anchor: والمراد من الحق هنا الصدق من حق الشيء إذا ثبت ، والصدق هو الثابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “with truth” can mean seriously and not as amusement, so the account should be recited with a proper purpose rather than for entertainment.
rows.anchor: ويصح أن يكون الحق ضد الباطل وهو الجد غير الهزل ، أي اتل هذا النبأ متلبسا بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may also warn against Israelite storytellers’ additions to the reasons one brother killed the other.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون قوله { بالحق } مشيرا إلى ما خف بالقصة من زيادات زادها أهل القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh is a temporal adverb attached to nabāʾ, locating the account at the time the two offered their sacrifices.
rows.anchor: أي خبرهما الحاصل وقت تقريبهما قربانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarrabā derives from qurbān, now a lexicalized noun originally meaning what one offers to God, such as charity, sacrifice, or prayer; it does not mean simply “brought near.”
rows.anchor: وفعل { قربا } هنا مشتق من القربان الذي صار بمنزلة الاسم الجامد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah names the brothers Cain and Abel, called Qabil and Habil in Arabic; Qabil farmed, while Habil herded sheep, and they offered crops and firstborn flock respectively.
rows.anchor: وفي التوراة هما ( قايين ) والعرب يسمونه قابيل وأخوه ( هابيل )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAshur says it is unknown whether offerings were distributed to the poor or left for people generally.
rows.anchor: ولا ندري هل كان القربان عندهم يعطى للفقراء ونحوهم أو كان يترك للناس عامة

words: فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted Habil’s offering, not Qabil’s; apparently God revealed that outcome to Adam.
rows.anchor: فتقبل الله قربان هابيل ولم يتقبل قربان قابيل . والظاهر أن قبول قربان أحدهما دون الآخر حصل بوحي من الله لآدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rejected Qabil’s offering because he was not righteous and had sins.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يتقبل الله قربان قابيل لأنه لم يكن رجلا صالحا بل كانت له خطايا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says Qabil was an unbeliever; Ibn ʿAshur rejects this because it conflicts with his making an offering.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان كافرا ، وهذا ينافي كونه يقرب قربانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular qurbān is generic: each brother made his own offering, rather than the two sharing one sacrifice.
rows.anchor: وأفرد القربان في الآية لإرادة الجنس ، وإنما قرب كل واحد منهما قربانا

words: فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not name which brother’s offering was accepted because identification adds nothing to the lesson.
rows.anchor: ولم يسم الله تعالى المتقبل منه والذي لم يتقبل منه إذ لا جدوى لذلك في موقع العبرة

words: فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jealousy over the distinction of acceptance drove the murder; envy was the first crime to appear on earth.
rows.anchor: وإنما حمله على قتل أخيه حسده على مزية القبول . والحسد أول جريمة ظهرت في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Habil’s reply is admonition and a disclaimer of any cause for murder: acceptance belongs to God and comes from the God-fearing, implicitly showing his brother was not pious and that the accepted offering gives no grounds for killing.
rows.anchor: وقوله في الجواب { إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين } موعظة وتعريض وتنصل مما يوجب قتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If muttaqūn has its ordinary religious sense, the claim restricts acceptance to the pious; that may have been their law, later superseded by Islam’s acceptance of a believer’s good deeds despite other lapses.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان المراد من المتقين معناه المعروف شرعا المحكي بلفظه الدال عليه مراد ابن آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes “pious” to mean sincere in the act, making nonacceptance evidence of insincerity; Ibn ʿAshur says this stretches the customary meaning of taqwa.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد بالمتقين المخلصون في العمل ، فيكون عدم القبول أمارة على عدم الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading understands acceptance as complete acceptance, indicated by a sacrifice being consumed by fire, like complete guidance for the pious and the full afterlife reserved for them.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد بالتقبل تقبلا خاصا ، وهو التقبل التام الدال عليه احتراق القربان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that the restriction concerns acceptance of sacrifices specifically.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد تقبل القرابين خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, piety means intending God-consciousness through the offering; Habil’s brother instead intended to boast, and acceptance in that sense was the law of their time.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد المتقين بالقربان ، أي المريدين به تقوى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Habil’s words warn his brother about the gravity of murder and imply he could defend himself but refrains out of fear of God.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { لئن بسطت إلي يدك لتقتلني } الخ موعظة لأخيه ليذكره خطر هذا الجرم

words: مَا أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAshur’s apparent reading is Habil’s own judgment that even killing in self-defense was a grave offense; he knew what killing meant from slaughter and hunting, and regarded life as sacred even for an unjust person.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا اجتهاد من هابيل في استعظام جرم قتل النفس ، ولو كان القتل دفاعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the brothers may have learned from Adam a charge to preserve every life, great or small, even when defending oneself.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكونا تلقيا من أبيهما الوصاية بحفظ النفوس صغيرها وكبيرها

words: مَا أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His fear of God suggests their law prohibited defense that caused the aggressor’s death; Ibn ʿAshur says this was abrogated, since later laws permit necessary self-defense without exceeding what is needed.
rows.anchor: فقوله : { إني أخاف الله } يدل على أن الدفاع بما يفضي إلى القتل كان محرما

words: مَا أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The hadith about two Muslims meeting with swords is about political conflict and struggle for dominance, where an attacker would stop if the other yielded, rather than a general prohibition on self-defense.
rows.anchor: وأما حديث ( إذا التقى المسلمان بسيفيهما فالقاتل والمقتول في النار ) فذلك في القتال على الملك

words: مَا أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To avoid civil strife, the Prophet ordered the better party to yield and bear the blame; ʿUthman took that position in hope of reconciliation.
rows.anchor: فأمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أصلح الفريقين بالتسليم للآخر وحمل التبعة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Urīdu means “I intend” regarding refraining from defense; irāda can mean resolve, as in Moses’ marriage proposal and the declaration that God intends ease.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { أريد } : أريد من إمساكي عن الدفاع . وأطلقت الإرادة على العزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause explains the preceding refusal; it is set apart and begins with inna to signal the causal force of the explanation.
rows.anchor: فالجملة تعليل للتي قبلها ، ولذلك فصلت وافتتحت ب ( إن ) المشعرة بالتعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabūʾ means “return,” figuratively “acquire” through one’s deed, as if the killer set out seeking gain but came away with two sins.
rows.anchor: و { تبوء } ترجع ، وهو رجوع مجازي ، أي تكتسب ذلك من فعلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stronger interpretation of “my sin” is Habil’s earlier sins during his life: he hopes they will be forgiven while the murderer bears his own and Habil’s burden.
rows.anchor: والأظهر في معنى قوله { بإثمي } ما له من الآثام الفارطة في عمره

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report in Muslim says the wrongdoer and wronged person meet on Judgment Day: the victim receives the wrongdoer’s good deeds until justice is done, or transfers sins to him if the wrongdoer has none.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( يؤتى بالظالم والمظلوم يوم القيامة فيؤخذ من حسنات الظالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Habil spoke from revealed knowledge, this matched the law later enacted in Islam; if he reasoned it himself, Ibn ʿAshur says his judgment was correct and inspired, almost like prophecy.
rows.anchor: فإن كان قد قال هذا عن علم من وحي فقد كان مثل ما شرع في الإسلام
